summary: Sustained first-byte lag on chat completions after serving runtime rebuild and model rebind
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sustained increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completions after a serving runtime rebuild (v2.4.0) and a model rebind that occurred in the morning deploy window. The symptom is most visible for short prompts and chat sessions that previously returned first tokens under ~120ms but now take 400ms–1.2s.

Impact:
- BrightWrite reports degraded UX in production affecting ~12% of chat requests (real-time assistant flows).
- Error rate not elevated; primarily higher latency and occasional client-side 504s when combined with retries.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east (pool-rw-3).
- Serving runtime: v2.4.0 (rebuild with new kernel-selection logic).
- Routing policy: latency_preferred with model-pin to rw-instruct-v2-8b-quant.
- Customer is on enterprise plan with Dedicated routing and reserved capacity.

Repro steps (observed by customer):
1) Start new chat session with a short system + user prompt (20–80 tokens total).
2) Call /v1/chat/completions with streaming enabled.
3) Observe first token delay; subsequent token throughput normal once the stream begins.

Observed metrics / logs:
- Median TTFB for affected customer window (2026-03-10 09:00–11:30 UTC): 720ms (baseline pre-deploy ~95ms).
- p95 TTFB: 1.05s.
- No consistent 5xx spikes; 504s occur when upstream retries and client timeout accumulate.
- Serving node logs show repeated kernel fallback warnings: "kernel_selector: no optimized kernel; falling back to generic path" on affected model shards.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped for pinned model sessions immediately after the rebind (from 87% to 15%).

Customer-provided artifacts:
- HAR of failing session (attached to the ticket).
- Example request IDs: req_us_east_7381f, req_us_east_73ac2, req_us_east_73b9e.

Expected behavior:
First token latency should remain within SLAs for dedicated capacity (<200ms median for these short prompts).
investigation_notes: 03/10 10:05 - Support triaged and validated increased TTFB from customer's traces and platform metrics.
03/10 10:30 - Routed to SRE because metric anomaly correlated with v2.4.0 runtime rollout to pool-rw-3.
03/10 11:00 - SRE observed kernel_selector warnings on a subset of GPU nodes; fallback to generic kernel increases per-token setup cost for first token.
03/10 12:15 - Noted KV cache invalidation for sessions that were pinned during model rebind; sessions requiring full KV rebuild show longer cold-start latencies.

03/10 13:40 - Hypotheses: (A) new kernel-selection heuristic incorrectly filters optimized kernels for quantized shard shapes; (B) model rebind caused stale cache entries leading to synchronous KV warm-up; (C) routing changes increased cross-node handoffs adding handshake overhead.
03/11 09:20 - Reproduced locally by forcing kernel_selector to emulate v2.4.0 decision path; reproduced TTFB increase on short prompts when optimized kernels are not chosen.
03/11 11:00 - Confirmed that forcing fallback to previous kernel list (from 2.3.7) returns TTFB to baseline in test harness.
comments: Support (Maya): Customer opened after noticing regressions post-deploy; provided traces and HAR. Asked for escalation to SRE.
SRE (Diego): Investigating; kernel_selector logs show repeated 'no optimized kernel' warnings on raylet-gpu-7 and raylet-gpu-9.
Engineering (Anya Patel): Early theory - the kernel signature hashing changed in the rebuild causing a mismatch with the optimization registry. Creating a hotfix PR to revert the signature check.

Customer (BrightWrite - Alex R.): We can temporarily pin traffic away from pool-rw-3 or accept a short maintenance window but need ETA on fix; some users are canceling sessions due to perceived slowness.
Support (Maya): Suggested customer pin to rw-chatlight-v1 variant as a short-term workaround; scheduled meeting with BrightWrite ops for 03/11 16:00 UTC to coordinate.
Engineering (Anya): PR created https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/1009 with kernel-selector revert; requesting canary in us-east on non-prod first.
resolution:
Workaround and next steps:
- 03/11 18:00 UTC: BrightWrite traffic temporarily routed to pool-rw-2 (older runtime v2.3.7) and TTFB returned to baseline; confirmed with customer.
- 03/12 02:30 UTC: Rolled hotfix v2.4.1 that reintroduces the previous kernel signature path and adds a telemetry flag to detect future mismatches.
- 03/12 04:10 UTC: Canary rollout validated on non-prod and then prod pool-rw-3; TTFB metrics restored (median ~110ms).
- 03/12 06:00 UTC: Hotfix promoted to all affected pools.

Follow-up actions:
- Engineering to add an automated check in CI that validates kernel-selector picks optimized kernels for common quantized shard shapes (owner: Anya Patel, due 2026-03-20).
- SRE to add alert for sudden KV cache hit-rate drops per model-pool (owner: Diego Alvarez, due 2026-03-16).
- Postmortem to be published in Confluence and linked once complete.
status_notes: Owner Diego Alvarez actively coordinating rollback and hotfix rollout; customer routed to alternate pool during mitigation. Awaiting postmortem and production monitoring confirmation before closing.
